summary.name: Vintage Rubber Hose Animation. An authored Motion Graphic in Animation Techniques: early sound-era hand-inked cel cartoon drawing with stepped, elastic acting; its only optional effects are film wear and a vintage film-leader countdown.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: strong irregular ink silhouettes, organic slightly imperfect contours with varied line weight, simplified forms, flat cel fills under bold painterly or cel shadow masses, expressive warped or asymmetric scenery and layered atmosphere. Characters, when present, may be any original subject with rounded elastic masses and jointless hose limbs; shots without characters are valid.
summary.decisionGuidance: Identity: early hand-inked cel cartoon drawing with irregular ink silhouettes, painterly shadow masses, expressive scenery and stepped elastic acting. Advantages: warm, playful, hand-made character and environment performance for any original subject, with optional film wear and a precise vintage leader for period flavour. Disadvantages: needs authored key drawings and consistent construction; it reads as nostalgic rather than sleek. Combination fit: stands alone; Traditional Cel Animation can supply drawn frames and data storytelling can add inked diagrams. Visual constraints: original subjects only, flat fills and ink contours, the project's palette first, no neon, glossy 3D or clean corporate vector icons unless requested.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: stories, intros, explainers and title moments that want an early hand-drawn cartoon feel, with or without characters. Inferred: brand, education and entertainment pieces built around an original subject. Not suited to photoreal, glossy 3D or clean corporate vector briefs. Audience is unspecified.
summary.limitations: Never imitate an existing cartoon character, mascot, recognizable silhouette or reference composition. No subject, story, setting or sequence is required. Avoid neon, glossy gradients and heavy saturation unless requested. Keep flashes to three per second or fewer; an optional film leader is a creative hybrid, not a strict historical reconstruction.
summary.palette: The project's palette comes first. Suggested default: ink black #25221F, aged ivory #F1E3C6, sepia brown #856548, dusty grey #77736D, muted rust #B5523A, vintage gold #E8B65B, faded teal #7EA9A3 and pale sky blue #B9D8D2. Black-and-white references inform drawing and film material, not a required grayscale look.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: stepped drawings, typically 12 per second against a 24 fps film reference, from absolute time; expressive elastic poses with anticipation, squash and stretch, overshoot, arcs and rhythmic timing; readable holds without a mandatory perpetual bounce. Optional effects only: film wear on the whole plate, and a leader with precise rings and crosshairs, a pale bold sans-serif numeral and a rotating clock-wipe sector.
summary.audio: Optional ideas governed by the project's audio settings: jazz percussion, upright bass, muted brass, playful woodwinds, cartoon sound effects, projector noise or vinyl hiss with film wear, and clicks with an optional leader. Do not invent narration or music when audio is disabled. The catalog preview is silent.
summary.assetRequirements: Subjects, any characters, story, copy, palette, duration, aspect ratio, resolution and frame rate come from the project. Everything can be code-drawn with system fonts; supplied hand-drawn cels can replace coded drawings. The drawing rate is animation sampling, not the delivery frame rate.
summary.combinations: Usually used alone. Traditional Cel Animation (style-081) can supply drawn cel frames; Scientific Visualization / Data Storytelling (style-097) can add explanatory diagrams in the same ink and palette.
summary.productionApproach: SVG and HTML/CSS draw ink, cels, scenery, any characters and text; Canvas 2D or SVG filters and Rough.js are added only for optional film wear or line boil. The optional leader is precise geometry kept separate from the cartoon artwork. GSAP drives one paused timeline through pure time-state functions. Composition and export follow the project renderer.
